QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_12

question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, Chinese Walls are implemented by a Cat III AIF primarily to:

answer.text: Separate the fund from its auditors.
Act as a physical vault for cash holdings.
Protect confidentiality and help avoid conflicts of interest.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 284 of the workbook, establishing appropriate Chinese walls protecting confidentiality is listed as a measure to avoid conflicts of interest within a Cat III AIF Manager. The Trap: Auditor independence and FEMA limits are unrelated to Chinese walls; the 'physical vault' option is the literal (not financial-industry) usage of the term. Note: Chinese walls are a confidentiality and conflict-management measure; the specific operational design depends on the manager's business model.
